sanskrit: abravīt kila dāśārha vairāṭīm ārjuniḥ purā mātulasya kulaṃ bhadre tava putro gamiṣyati
english: O Dāśārha, long ago the son of Arjuna said to the daughter of Virāṭa: 'O blessed one, your son shall journey to the house of his maternal uncle.'

sanskrit: gatvā vṛṣṇyandhakakulaṃ dhanurvedaṃ grahīṣyati astrāṇi ca vicitrāṇi nītiśāstraṃ ca kevalam
english: 'Having gone to the house of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, he shall acquire the science of archery, and weapons of many wondrous kinds, and the whole science of statecraft.'

sanskrit: ity etat praṇayāt tāta saubhadraḥ paravīrahā kathayām āsa durdharṣas tathā caitan na saṃśayaḥ
english: Thus out of love, dear one, did the son of Subhadrā speak — that slayer of enemy heroes, that unassailable one — and so shall it surely be, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: tās tvāṃ vayaṃ praṇamyeha yācāmo madhusūdana kulasyāsya hitārthaṃ tvaṃ kuru kalyāṇam uttamam
english: Bowing before you here, O slayer of Madhu, we beseech you: for the welfare of this lineage, work this supreme deliverance.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vārṣṇeyaṃ pṛthā pṛthulalocanā ucchritya bāhū duḥkhārtā tāś cānyāḥ prāpatan bhuvi
english: Having spoken thus to the Vārṣṇeya, the large-eyed Pṛthā, stricken with grief, raised up her arms, and she and the other women fell to the ground.

sanskrit: abruvaṃś ca mahārāja sarvāḥ sāsrāvilekṣaṇāḥ svasrīyo vāsudevasya mṛto jāta iti prabho
english: And, O great king, they all cried out, their eyes clouded with tears: 'The grandnephew of Vāsudeva is born dead, O lord!'

sanskrit: evam ukte tataḥ kuntīṃ pratyagṛhṇāj janārdanaḥ bhūmau nipatitāṃ caināṃ sāntvayām āsa bhārata
english: When this was spoken, Janārdana lifted up Kuntī, who had fallen to the earth, and consoled her, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca utthitāyāṃ pṛthāyāṃ tu subhadrā bhrātaraṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā cukrośa duḥkhārtā vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Pṛthā had risen, Subhadrā, beholding her brother, wailed aloud, stricken with grief, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkākṣa paśyasva pautraṃ pārthasya dhīmataḥ parikṣīṇeṣu kuruṣu parikṣīṇaṃ gatāyuṣam
english: O lotus-eyed one, behold the grandson of the wise Pārtha — born wasted away among the wasted Kurus, his life already gone.

sanskrit: iṣīkā droṇaputreṇa bhīmasenārtham udyatā sottarāyāṃ nipatitā vijaye mayi caiva ha
english: The reed-weapon hurled by the son of Droṇa, aimed against Bhīmasena, has fallen instead upon Uttarā, upon victory itself, and upon me.

sanskrit: seyaṃ jvalantī hṛdaye mayi tiṣṭhati keśava yan na paśyāmi durdharṣa mama putrasutaṃ vibho
english: That same fire stands blazing within my heart, O Keśava, since I do not see, O unassailable lord, the son of my son.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyati dharmātmā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenārjunau cāpi mādravatyāḥ sutau ca tau
english: What now will the righteous Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira say, and Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and those two sons of Mādrī?

sanskrit: śrutvābhimanyos tanayaṃ jātaṃ ca mṛtam eva ca muṣitā iva vārṣṇeya droṇaputreṇa pāṇḍavāḥ
english: When they hear that Abhimanyu's son is both born and dead, O Vārṣṇeya, the Pāṇḍavas will feel as though robbed by the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: abhimanyuḥ priyaḥ kṛṣṇa pitṝṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ te śrutvā kiṃ nu vakṣyanti droṇaputrāstranirjitāḥ
english: Abhimanyu was dear to his fathers, O Kṛṣṇa — of this there is no doubt. What will they say, undone by the weapon of Droṇa's son?

sanskrit: bhavitātaḥ paraṃ duḥkhaṃ kiṃ nu manye janārdana abhimanyoḥ sutāt kṛṣṇa mṛtāj jātād ariṃdama
english: What grief greater than this can there be, I wonder, O Janārdana, than this — the son of Abhimanyu born dead, O Kṛṣṇa, O subduer of foes?

sanskrit: sāhaṃ prasādaye kṛṣṇa tvām adya śirasā natā pṛtheyaṃ draupadī caiva tāḥ paśya puruṣottama
english: I, then, bow my head and entreat you today, O Kṛṣṇa — Pṛthā here too, and Draupadī. Look upon them, O best of men.

sanskrit: yadā droṇasuto garbhān pāṇḍūnāṃ hanti mādhava tadā kila tvayā drauṇiḥ kruddhenokto 'rimardana
english: When the son of Droṇa slew the unborn children of the Pāṇḍavas, O Mādhava, then, in your wrath, you spoke to that son of Droṇa, O crusher of foes:

sanskrit: akāmaṃ tvā kariṣyāmi brahmabandho narādhama ahaṃ saṃjīvayiṣyāmi kirīṭitanayātmajam
english: 'Against your will I shall thwart you, O degraded Brāhmaṇa, O basest of men: I shall restore to life the son of the son of the Diademed One.'

sanskrit: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā jānamānā balaṃ tava prasādaye tvā durdharṣa jīvatām abhimanyujaḥ
english: Having heard this word of yours, and knowing your power, I entreat you, O unassailable one: let the son of Abhimanyu live.

sanskrit: yady evaṃ tvaṃ pratiśrutya na karoṣi vacaḥ śubham saphalaṃ vṛṣṇiśārdūla mṛtāṃ mām upadhāraya
english: If, having so promised, you do not make good that auspicious word, O tiger of the Vṛṣṇis, then know me to be as good as dead.

sanskrit: abhimanyoḥ suto vīra na saṃjīvati yady ayam jīvati tvayi durdharṣa kiṃ kariṣyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: O hero, if this son of Abhimanyu does not return to life — when, O unassailable one, he could live through you — what use shall I then have for you?

sanskrit: saṃjīvayainaṃ durdharṣa mṛtaṃ tvam abhimanyujam sadṛśākṣasutaṃ vīra sasyaṃ varṣann ivāmbudaḥ
english: Restore him to life, O unassailable one — this dead son of Abhimanyu, child of his like-eyed son, O hero — as a rain-cloud revives the parched grain by its showers.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi keśava dharmātmā satyavān satyavikramaḥ sa tāṃ vācam ṛtāṃ kartum arhasi tvam ariṃdama
english: For you, O Keśava, are righteous of soul, truthful, and true in valor; you ought, O subduer of foes, to make that word come true.

sanskrit: icchann api hi lokāṃs trīñ jīvayethā mṛtān imān kiṃ punar dayitaṃ jātaṃ svasrīyasyātmajaṃ mṛtam
english: For if you so willed, you could restore to life all the dead in the three worlds; how much more this beloved newborn, the dead son of your grandnephew.

sanskrit: prabhāvajñāsmi te kṛṣṇa tasmād etad bravīmi te kuruṣva pāṇḍuputrāṇām imaṃ param anugraham
english: I know your power, O Kṛṣṇa, and therefore I say this to you: grant the sons of Pāṇḍu this supreme favor.

sanskrit: svaseti vā mahābāho hataputreti vā punaḥ prapannā mām iyaṃ veti dayāṃ kartum ihārhasi
english: Whether as 'my sister,' O mighty-armed one, or 'she whose son is slain,' or 'she who has taken refuge in me' — by any of these you ought here to show compassion.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu rājendra keśihā duḥkhamūrchitaḥ tatheti vyājahāroccair hlādayann iva taṃ janam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, O lord of kings, the slayer of Keśin, overcome with grief, declared aloud 'So be it!' — as if gladdening that gathered company.

sanskrit: vākyena tena hi tadā taṃ janaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ hlādayām āsa sa vibhur gharmārtaṃ salilair iva
english: By that word the bull among men, that mighty lord, then refreshed those people as water refreshes those tormented by heat.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prāviśat tūrṇaṃ janmaveśma pitus tava arcitaṃ puruṣavyāghra sitair mālyair yathāvidhi
english: Then he swiftly entered the birth-chamber of your father, O tiger among men — a chamber duly honored with white garlands.

sanskrit: apāṃ kumbhaiḥ supūrṇaiś ca vinyastaiḥ sarvatodiśam ghṛtena tindukālātaiḥ sarṣapaiś ca mahābhuja
english: With pots brimful of water set out on every side, with clarified butter, with firebrands of tinduka wood and with mustard seeds, O mighty-armed one,

sanskrit: śastraiś ca vimalair nyastaiḥ pāvakaiś ca samantataḥ vṛddhābhiś cābhirāmābhiḥ paricārārtham acyutaḥ
english: with bright weapons laid about and fires kindled all around, and with comely old women set there for attendance — so the Unfallen One beheld it,

sanskrit: dakṣaiś ca parito vīra bhiṣagbhiḥ kuśalais tathā dadarśa ca sa tejasvī rakṣoghnāny api sarvaśaḥ dravyāṇi sthāpitāni sma vidhivat kuśalair janaiḥ
english: and surrounded by skilled and able physicians, O hero. And that glorious one saw too the demon-banishing substances of every kind, set in their proper places by knowing hands.

sanskrit: tathāyuktaṃ ca tad dṛṣṭvā janmaveśma pitus tava hṛṣṭo 'bhavad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt
english: Seeing the birth-chamber of your father so well prepared, Hṛṣīkeśa was gladdened, and cried out, 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: tathā bruvati vārṣṇeye prahṛṣṭavadane tadā draupadī tvaritā gatvā vairāṭīṃ vākyam abravīt
english: As the Vārṣṇeya spoke thus, his face all gladness, Draupadī hastened to the daughter of Virāṭa and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ayam āyāti te bhadre śvaśuro madhusūdanaḥ purāṇarṣir acintyātmā samīpam aparājitaḥ
english: 'O blessed one, here comes to you your father-in-law, the slayer of Madhu — the ancient seer, of inconceivable being, the unconquered.'

sanskrit: sāpi bāṣpakalāṃ vācaṃ nigṛhyāśrūṇi caiva ha susaṃvītābhavad devī devavat kṛṣṇam īkṣatī
english: And she, restraining her tear-choked voice and her very tears, that lady drew her garments close about her, gazing upon Kṛṣṇa as upon a god.

sanskrit: sā tathā dūyamānena hṛdayena tapasvinī dṛṣṭvā govindam āyāntaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: With her heart thus burning, the suffering woman, beholding Govinda draw near, lamented piteously:

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkākṣa paśyasva bālāv iha vinākṛtau abhimanyuṃ ca māṃ caiva hatau tulyaṃ janārdana
english: 'O lotus-eyed one, look upon these two children left bereft — Abhimanyu and myself — slain alike, O Janārdana.'

sanskrit: vārṣṇeya madhuhan vīra śirasā tvāṃ prasādaye droṇaputrāstranirdagdhaṃ jīvayainaṃ mamātmajam
english: 'O Vārṣṇeya, O slayer of Madhu, O hero, I bow my head and entreat you: bring back to life this son of mine, scorched by the weapon of Droṇa's son.'

sanskrit: yadi sma dharmarājñā vā bhīmasenena vā punaḥ tvayā vā puṇḍarīkākṣa vākyam uktam idaṃ bhavet
english: 'If by the Dharmarāja, or by Bhīmasena, or by you, O lotus-eyed one, such a word as this had been spoken —'

sanskrit: ajānatīm iṣīkeyaṃ janitrīṃ hantv iti prabho aham eva vinaṣṭā syāṃ nedam evaṃgataṃ bhavet
english: '"Let this reed-weapon slay the unknowing mother," O lord — then I myself would have perished, and matters would not have come to this pass.'

sanskrit: garbhasthasyāsya bālasya brahmāstreṇa nipātanam kṛtvā nṛśaṃsaṃ durbuddhir drauṇiḥ kiṃ phalam aśnute
english: 'By the cruel deed of felling this child in the womb with the Brahmā-weapon, what fruit does that evil-minded son of Droṇa reap?'

sanskrit: sā tvā prasādya śirasā yāce śatrunibarhaṇa prāṇāṃs tyakṣyāmi govinda nāyaṃ saṃjīvate yadi
english: 'I bow my head and entreat you, O destroyer of foes: I shall give up my life, O Govinda, if this child does not return to life.'

sanskrit: asmin hi bahavaḥ sādho ye mamāsan manorathāḥ te droṇaputreṇa hatāḥ kiṃ nu jīvāmi keśava
english: 'For all the many hopes that were mine, O noble one, vested in this child, have been slain by the son of Droṇa. Why then should I live, O Keśava?'

sanskrit: āsīn mama matiḥ kṛṣṇa pūrṇotsaṅgā janārdana abhivādayiṣye diṣṭyeti tad idaṃ vitathīkṛtam
english: 'It was my thought, O Kṛṣṇa, my lap full at last, O Janārdana: "I shall make him salute you and rejoice, by fortune's grace" — and that has now been made vain.'

sanskrit: capalākṣasya dāyāde mṛte 'smin puruṣarṣabha viphalā me kṛtāḥ kṛṣṇa hṛdi sarve manorathāḥ
english: 'Now that this heir of the restless-eyed one lies dead, O bull among men, all the hopes within my heart, O Kṛṣṇa, are made fruitless.'

sanskrit: capalākṣaḥ kilātīva priyas te madhusūdana sutaṃ paśyasva tasyemaṃ brahmāstreṇa nipātitam
english: 'The restless-eyed one was, they say, exceedingly dear to you, O slayer of Madhu: look upon this his son, struck down by the Brahmā-weapon.'

sanskrit: kṛtaghno 'yaṃ nṛśaṃso 'yaṃ yathāsya janakas tathā yaḥ pāṇḍavīṃ śriyaṃ tyaktvā gato 'dya yamasādanam
english: 'Ungrateful is this child, and cruel, even as his begetter was — he who, forsaking the Pāṇḍava fortune, has gone today to the abode of Yama.'

sanskrit: mayā caitat pratijñātaṃ raṇamūrdhani keśava abhimanyau hate vīra tvām eṣyāmy acirād iti
english: 'And this I vowed at the forefront of battle, O Keśava: "When Abhimanyu is slain, O hero, I shall follow you ere long."'

sanskrit: tac ca nākaravaṃ kṛṣṇa nṛśaṃsā jīvitapriyā idānīm āgatāṃ tatra kiṃ nu vakṣyati phālguniḥ
english: 'And that I did not do, O Kṛṣṇa — cruel, and clinging to life. What now will the son of Phalguna say to me when I come to him there?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saivaṃ vilapya karuṇaṃ sonmādeva tapasvinī uttarā nyapatad bhūmau kṛpaṇā putragṛddhinī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus piteously lamented, the suffering Uttarā, as though distraught, fell wretchedly to the ground, yearning for her son.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā nipatitāṃ hatabandhuparicchadām cukrośa kuntī duḥkhārtā sarvāś ca bharatastriyaḥ
english: Beholding her fallen, stripped of kin and of all that adorned her, Kuntī cried out, stricken with grief, and all the women of the Bhāratas with her.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tad rājan pāṇḍavānāṃ niveśanam aprekṣaṇīyam abhavad ārtasvaranināditam
english: For a while, O king, the dwelling of the Pāṇḍavas became a thing one could not bear to look upon, resounding with cries of anguish.

sanskrit: sā muhūrtaṃ ca rājendra putraśokābhipīḍitā kaśmalābhihatā vīra vairāṭī tv abhavat tadā
english: And for a while, O lord of kings, the daughter of Virāṭa, tormented by grief for her son, lay overcome by a swoon, O hero.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tu sā saṃjñām uttarā bharatarṣabha aṅkam āropya taṃ putram idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: But when Uttarā had regained her senses, O bull of the Bhāratas, she set that son upon her lap and spoke these words:

sanskrit: dharmajñasya sutaḥ saṃs tvam adharmam avabudhyase yas tvaṃ vṛṣṇipravīrasya kuruṣe nābhivādanam
english: 'Being the son of one who knew righteousness, do you yet take to unrighteousness — you who offer no salutation to the foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis?'

sanskrit: putra gatvā mama vaco brūyās tvaṃ pitaraṃ tava durmaraṃ prāṇināṃ vīra kāle prāpte kathaṃ cana
english: 'O son, going to your father, speak my word to him: "Hard is it, O hero, for living beings to die in any way until their appointed time has come."'

sanskrit: yāhaṃ tvayā vihīnādya patyā putreṇa caiva ha martavye sati jīvāmi hatasvastir akiṃcanā
english: 'For I, bereft today of you — both husband and son — though death were fitting, yet live on, robbed of all blessing, possessed of nothing.'

sanskrit: atha vā dharmarājñāham anujñātā mahābhuja bhakṣayiṣye viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pravekṣye vā hutāśanam
english: 'Or, with the leave of the Dharmarāja, O mighty-armed one, I shall swallow a sharp poison, or enter the devouring fire.'

sanskrit: atha vā durmaraṃ tāta yad idaṃ me sahasradhā patiputravihīnāyā hṛdayaṃ na vidīryate
english: 'Yet hard it is to die, my dear, since this heart of mine, bereft of husband and son, does not burst asunder into a thousand pieces.'

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha putra paśyemāṃ duḥkhitāṃ prapitāmahīm ārtām upaplutāṃ dīnāṃ nimagnāṃ śokasāgare
english: 'Rise, my son, and look upon this grieving great-grandmother — anguished, overwhelmed, forlorn, sunk in an ocean of sorrow.'

sanskrit: āryāṃ ca paśya pāñcālīṃ sātvatīṃ ca tapasvinīm māṃ ca paśya suduḥkhārtāṃ vyādhaviddhāṃ mṛgīm iva
english: 'Behold too the noble Pāñcālī, and the suffering daughter of the Sātvatas, and behold me, sore stricken with grief, like a doe pierced by the hunter.'

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha paśya vadanaṃ lokanāthasya dhīmataḥ puṇḍarīkapalāśākṣaṃ pureva capalekṣaṇam
english: 'Rise, and behold the face of the wise Lord of the worlds, its eyes like lotus-petals, restless-glancing as of old.'

sanskrit: evaṃ vipralapantīṃ tu dṛṣṭvā nipatitāṃ punaḥ uttarāṃ tāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ punar utthāpayanty uta
english: Seeing Uttarā thus lamenting and again fallen, all those women once more raised her up.

sanskrit: utthāya tu punar dhairyāt tadā matsyapateḥ sutā prāñjaliḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ bhūmāv evābhyavādayat
english: Then, recovering her composure and rising, the daughter of the Matsya king, with hands joined in reverence, saluted the lotus-eyed one upon the very ground.

sanskrit: śrutvā sa tasyā vipulaṃ vilāpaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ upaspṛśya tataḥ kṛṣṇo brahmāstraṃ saṃjahāra tat
english: Having heard her abundant lament, that bull among men, Kṛṣṇa, sipped water in purification and then withdrew that Brahmā-weapon.

sanskrit: pratijajñe ca dāśārhas tasya jīvitam acyutaḥ abravīc ca viśuddhātmā sarvaṃ viśrāvayañ jagat
english: And the Dāśārha, the Unfallen One, vowed the child's life, and, pure of soul, he spoke, making all the world to hear:

sanskrit: na bravīmy uttare mithyā satyam etad bhaviṣyati eṣa saṃjīvayāmy enaṃ paśyatāṃ sarvadehinām
english: 'I do not speak falsely, O Uttarā: this shall come true. I do here restore this child to life before the eyes of all embodied beings.'

sanskrit: noktapūrvaṃ mayā mithyā svaireṣv api kadā cana na ca yuddhe parāvṛttas tathā saṃjīvatām ayam
english: 'Never before have I spoken falsely, not even in jest, nor have I ever turned my back in battle: by that truth, let this child live.'

sanskrit: yathā me dayito dharmo brāhmaṇāś ca viśeṣataḥ abhimanyoḥ suto jāto mṛto jīvatv ayaṃ tathā
english: 'As righteousness is dear to me, and the Brāhmaṇas above all — by that truth, let this son of Abhimanyu, born dead, live again.'

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ nābhijānāmi vijayena kadā cana virodhaṃ tena satyena mṛto jīvatv ayaṃ śiśuḥ
english: 'As I have never known any quarrel with Vijaya at any time — by that truth, let this dead infant live.'

sanskrit: yathā satyaṃ ca dharmaś ca mayi nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitau tathā mṛtaḥ śiśur ayaṃ jīvatām abhimanyujaḥ
english: 'As truth and righteousness are ever established in me — even so, let this dead infant, the son of Abhimanyu, live.'

sanskrit: yathā kaṃsaś ca keśī ca dharmeṇa nihatau mayā tena satyena bālo 'yaṃ punar ujjīvatām iha
english: 'As Kaṃsa and Keśin were slain by me through righteousness — by that truth, let this child here come back again to life.'

sanskrit: ity ukto vāsudevena sa bālo bharatarṣabha śanaiḥ śanair mahārāja prāspandata sacetanaḥ
english: Thus spoken over by Vāsudeva, that child, O bull of the Bhāratas, little by little, O great king, began to stir, returning to consciousness.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca brahmāstraṃ tu yadā rājan kṛṣṇena pratisaṃhṛtam tadā tad veśma te pitrā tejasābhividīpitam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the Brahmā-weapon, O king, was withdrawn by Kṛṣṇa, then that chamber was lit up with the splendor of your father.

sanskrit: tato rakṣāṃsi sarvāṇi neśus tyaktvā gṛhaṃ tu tat antarikṣe ca vāg āsīt sādhu keśava sādhv iti
english: Then all the demons, forsaking that house, fled away, and a voice came from the sky: 'Well done, O Keśava, well done!'

sanskrit: tad astraṃ jvalitaṃ cāpi pitāmaham agāt tadā tataḥ prāṇān punar lebhe pitā tava janeśvara vyaceṣṭata ca bālo 'sau yathotsāhaṃ yathābalam
english: And that blazing weapon then departed to the Grandfather, and thereupon your father regained his breath, O lord of men, and that child stirred according to his vigor and strength.

sanskrit: babhūvur muditā rājaṃs tatas tā bharatastriyaḥ brāhmaṇān vācayām āsur govindasya ca śāsanāt
english: Then the women of the Bhāratas were filled with joy, O king, and at Govinda's command they had the Brāhmaṇas recite their blessings.

sanskrit: tatas tā muditāḥ sarvāḥ praśaśaṃsur janārdanam striyo bharatasiṃhānāṃ nāvaṃ labdhveva pāragāḥ
english: Then all those women, rejoicing, praised Janārdana — the women of the lions among the Bhāratas — like folk who reach the far shore on finding a boat.

sanskrit: kuntī drupadaputrī ca subhadrā cottarā tathā striyaś cānyā nṛsiṃhānāṃ babhūvur hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
english: Kuntī, and the daughter of Drupada, and Subhadrā, and Uttarā, and the other women of those lions among men became glad of heart.
